_why: Issue #115: what a real PMS does with an account's ALLOW list ('label=' / 'contentRating=' conditions),
the grouping question pms_share_filter_boolean_semantics.json could not settle, and whether reading
items AS a restricted account leaves out what its allow list hides.
Measured by writing one managed Home account's filterMovies/filterTelevision (PUT /api/users/{id}),
waiting for the PMS to apply it, then reading AS that account with its own server token. Only that
account's filters were written; each original value was restored byte-identical afterwards.
Conclusions the code relies on:
1. GROUPING. A filter is '&'-separated groups of '|'-separated alternatives: (A|B)&C. Case
'XYZNOPE&recommended|G' returned 0 movies; strict left-to-right would have returned 401. So '|'
binds TIGHTER than '&' — the question the #116 recording left open.
2. '&' is a strict AND even between two allow conditions: 'contentRating=G&label=<row>' shows nothing.
3. OWN ROW UNDER AN ALLOW LIST. Adding the row's label as an alternative in EVERY allow group shows the
row on Home and in the library, and inside it exactly the items the allow list admits. Added to
only one of two allow groups, the row stays hidden.
READ THAT LITERALLY (re-measured 2026-09-18, managed account, 'label=recommended' = 11 of 9,991
movies with none of them in the row): 'exactly the items the allow list admits' was ZERO. A share
filter matches ITEMS by label and a row's member titles carry no shortlist_ label — only the
collection does — so admitting the row's label cannot admit its contents. The account gets an EMPTY
row. The row collection itself also stayed visible in all three states, so the 'stays hidden until
admitted' part did not reproduce on PMS 1.43.3.10793 at all.
Do NOT read this conclusion as 'the account can then use its row'. See the review backlog entry of
2026-09-18. Beware also of the trap that voided the first attempt: 'label=Overlay' is on 9,980 of
9,991 movies on that server, so it admits the whole library and measures nothing.
4. READING AS THE ACCOUNT. GET /library/metadata/{k1,k2,...} with the account's token returns only
the keys its share filter admits (200, the rest silently absent), and 404 when it admits none —
the same shape as a batch of deleted keys (pms_metadata_batch_partial.json). plexapi's fetchItems
raises NotFound for that 404. An allow list on filterMovies does not touch TV items.
Row labels here: ROW = the probed person's shortlist_ label; OURS = the account's real exclude clause
(every other person's shortlist_ label). Library: 9,988 movies, 401 rated G, 11 labelled
'recommended', 6,660 not rated R.

5. A library the account is not shared behaves the same: its items are absent from a 200, and 404 when the batch holds only those. So one title's copy in an unshared library reads as hidden even when the account can see its copy in another library.
note_on_children: GET /library/collections/{key}/children does NOT apply the share filter (it returned every member of a row the account could not see); /library/metadata/{key}/children does.

cases.verdict: an allow list with no row label hides the person's own rows
row label as an alternative in the allow group: rows show, holding exactly the admitted items
row label added to a label= allow clause: row listed, contents still filtered
two allow groups, row label in both: row shows
two allow groups, row label in only one: row hidden

library_not_shared_with_the_account._why: Read-only, as a real account shared libraries 1 and 2 but not 12 ('Sports'), whose TV filter holds only label!= excludes. Items of a library the account is not shared are left out exactly like filtered ones; a batch of only those is a 404, never a 401/403.
